title: Insertion Sort
intuition: Builds a sorted array one element at a time by sliding each new element left into its correct slot.
whyExists: Highly efficient on small datasets ($n < 20$) and nearly-sorted arrays ($O(n)$ time), serving as the base case in hybrid algorithms like Timsort.
analogy: Sorting playing cards in your hand as they are dealt: picking each new card and sliding it between cards of lower and higher rank.
coreIdea: Picks the next element as key = a[i], shifts all preceding elements that are strictly greater than key one position to the right, and drops key into the opened gap at j + 1.

complexity.reason: Only compares and shifts elements that are strictly inverted.

pitfalls: Overwriting a[i] before saving it into the temporary key variable.
Off-by-one underflow when j reaches -1 in the while loop.
Performing unnecessary full swaps instead of single-direction right shifts.
